#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A complete hyp-prototype walkthrough in a throwaway directory, using only
# commands from SKILL.md. Run with HYP=/path/to/hyp to use a specific binary.
set -euo pipefail

HYP=${HYP:-hyp}
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
cd "$work"

# First word of a write command's output is the new node's display id.
id() { "$HYP" "$@" | awk '{print $1}'; }

export HYP_ACTOR=investigator-1
"$HYP" init
goal=$(id add goal --title "Dashboard loads in under 1 s on seed data" --why "owner request")
q=$(id add dq --parent "$goal" --title "Where should totals be computed?" --why "slow page")
h1=$(id add hyp --parent "$q" --title "Precompute totals in a nightly job" --why "rival A")
h2=$(id add hyp --parent "$q" --title "Compute totals per request with an index" --why "rival B")
e=$(id add exp --parent "$h1" --title "Read both designs against the page's query" --recipe none --decided-by reading --target "$h2" --why "excludes one rival")

mkdir -p ".tree/evidence/$e"
echo "nightly: the page reads one totals row; per-request: the page sums every order row on each load" > ".tree/evidence/$e/notes.txt"
"$HYP" record --exp "$e" --verdict "$h1=supports" --verdict "$h2=contradicts" \
  --observation "Precomputed totals are one row read; per-request sums every order row on each load" \
  --evidence ".tree/evidence/$e/notes.txt" --why "read both designs"

"$HYP" select "$q"
"$HYP" select "$q" "$h1" --why "only supported candidate"
"$HYP" confirm "$q" --role verifier --verdict sufficient --why "the notes exclude rival B" --actor verifier-1
## 9. Sandbox lifecycle and steps

This section is the authority for when hyp runs a recipe's commands and whether a sandbox exists when it does. The words are defined in [glossary.md](glossary.md), and the decision behind the section is [ADR 0001](adr/0001-hyp-runs-every-recipe-command.md) (#148). `skills/hyp-verification/RECIPE-FORMAT.md` says how to write a recipe that follows it.

### 9.1 Steps and sections

A bundle's `recipe.md` has one level-2 section per step (Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, Cleanup) and may have a Standalone section, which is not a step. A line in one of these sections that starts with `Run:`, outside a code fence, is a **command**: one script inside the bundle followed by fixed words. The section a command sits under decides when hyp runs it and whether a sandbox exists then. A command carries no other label, except that a Standalone command is named: `Run NAME: ./script WORDS`, with NAME matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*` and used once in the file. A plain `Run:` line under Standalone, a named line under any other heading, and a `Run:` line under a heading that is not one of the six are refused.

| Section | Does a sandbox exist? | When hyp runs it |
|---|---|---|
| Launch | yes | `hyp sandbox create`, for each recipe in stack order |
| Doctor | yes | `hyp sandbox create`, right after the same recipe's Launch |
| Drive | yes | `hyp sandbox drive ID`, between create and remove, for each recipe in stack order; it can be run again |
| Cleanup | yes | `hyp sandbox remove`, the last recipe first; also `hyp sandbox create`, after a failed Launch or Doctor |
| Evidence | no: it reads the kept files after remove | `hyp recipe evidence --record DIR REF OUT_DIR`, after remove, the first time and again on demand, also from a later version of the recipe; `hyp sandbox remove` never runs it. An OUT_DIR without `sandbox.json` exits 2, and the refusal names a Standalone command (`hyp recipe run`) for files no sandbox wrote |
| Standalone | no sandbox at all | `hyp recipe run --record DIR REF NAME ARGS` |

Evidence that the operator gathers by hand while the sandbox exists is not a command, and is unchanged: it is the files saved under `.tree/evidence/<E-id>/`. Scripted Evidence is the same step done by a command, which is why it runs after Cleanup: it reads only the kept files, so it can be run again.

A sandbox is a directory plus its record, not process isolation. Each command hyp starts leads its own process group, which its row records as `pgid` (ADR 0002). After Cleanup, `hyp sandbox remove` stops the groups of the Launch, Doctor, Drive and Cleanup commands that still have members: SIGTERM, up to 5 seconds, then SIGKILL. A timeout or Ctrl-C kills the running command's group (its row says `interrupted` for Ctrl-C), and an Evidence or Standalone group ends with its command; create still runs Cleanup after a Ctrl-C. Limits: a daemon that leaves its group, as Postgres's postmaster does by calling `setsid`, still needs its recipe's Cleanup, and the leftover check still applies; a group id reused after its group ended is not told apart; what a check cannot see is listed under §7.6 and ADR 0003. "Runs in a sandbox" means only that the command runs while the sandbox exists and gets that sandbox's `HYP_SANDBOX_*` variables (§9.3).

### 9.2 hyp runs every command

hyp runs every command in a bundle, and the operator runs none of a bundle's scripts directly. A command is what a `Run:` line names; every other file in the bundle, a helper script included, is hashed content (ADR 0002). Hashing never parses: a bundle whose `recipe.md` breaks a command rule, such as a `Run:` line outside a section or shell syntax, still hashes, so every pin to it still verifies, and `hyp check` names it as a bundle that does not open. `hyp recipe new` writes `format: 1` into every copy it makes, the one recipe format, and the line is a required field. Every use of a bundle without it is refused with exit 1, reading only its frontmatter: `hyp add exp`, `hyp sandbox create`, `hyp recipe run`, `hyp recipe evidence`, `hyp recipe known-answers`, and `hyp record --evidence` into such a bundle. The refusal names `hyp recipe new` as the way to copy it. `hyp recipe hash` still hashes it (ADR 0002, ADR 0007). `hyp recipe check` names each versioned bundle `frozen` when a tree pins its current hash, so its bytes never change, and `draft` when none does. When the repository root holds `go.mod`, `hyp recipe check` warns about each `.go` file in a versioned bundle, and `hyp add exp --recipe` about each one in the bundle it pins, because `go vet ./...` reads a `recipes/<name>@<N>/` directory holding one as a package outside the main module; the warning suggests a non-`.go` name, such as `x.go.txt`, and both commands still exit 0 (#258).

A recipe is self-contained when it relies on nothing but its own files, hyp and the subject, wherever its commands run. Self-contained does not mean "runs in the sandbox": a Standalone or scripted Evidence command is self-contained and runs with no sandbox. A fixed input that is not the subject, such as a fixture or a cases file, is a file of the bundle, so the recipe pin hashes it, and the code that reads it is in the bundle too. A file outside the bundle is the subject, or a read or write that the command's `External:` line names (ADR 0008, owner decision on #272, 2026-11-01). hyp does not detect a fixture outside the bundle.

Each Evidence and Standalone command states its reach on one line `External: TEXT` directly under its `Run:` line in `recipe.md`: the subject arguments and any outside reads or writes, or `none`. The line is no field `recipe.Load` requires, so a frozen bundle without it still loads and records. `hyp recipe check` warns `<command>: no External: line` for a command without one and `<command>: External: not stated (TODO)` for one whose text is empty or `TODO`, and exits as before. `hyp recipe new` writes `External: TODO` under each such command of the copy that has no line.

hyp's Go learns no replay concepts (#45). It runs a script with its arguments and records the exit code and the output. hyp is not a job runner: no retries, no background jobs and no stdin streaming.

### 9.3 How a command runs

- No shell runs a command. Its first word is a relative path containing `/` to an executable script inside the bundle, and the rest are plain words; quotes, `$`, pipes, redirects and globs are refused.
- Launch, Doctor and Cleanup run with the recipe's copy in the sandbox as their working directory, and get `HYP_SANDBOX_ID`, `HYP_SANDBOX_WT`, `HYP_SANDBOX_TMP`, `HYP_SANDBOX_RECIPE_TMP`, `HYP_SANDBOX_INPUTS` (the sandbox's copy of `--inputs FILE`, when given) and a `PATH` that starts with the sandbox hyp. They also inherit the environment of the process that runs hyp.
- Drive commands run like Launch: in the recipe's copy, with the sandbox's variables. They take no arguments from the operator; a Drive reads per-run values from the inputs file or from the state its Launch wrote.
- Evidence and Standalone commands are checks, and run exactly as their known-answer cases do (ADR 0003). They get no `HYP_SANDBOX_*` variables, because no sandbox exists when they run, and inherit nothing else of the caller's environment: only `PATH` (the copy of the running hyp the gate used, first, then the caller's `PATH`), a scratch `HOME` and `TMPDIR`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `HYP_OUT`, an empty directory for the files the check leaves; stdin is `/dev/null`. They run from a temporary copy of the bundle whose hash equals the library's, deleted afterwards, in an empty working directory of their own. A hyp killed while it runs leaves that copy (`hyp-run-*` under the system temp directory): hyp never reads it again and does not clean it up, the system's temp cleaning removes it, and the operator may delete it. An Evidence command gets the absolute OUT_DIR appended as its last argument; a Standalone command gets the caller's ARGS appended after its fixed words, as given, so a path in them must be absolute.
- Launch and Doctor together have 10 minutes for each recipe, and each Cleanup command has 2 minutes. Each Drive command has 60 minutes, each Evidence command 10 minutes, and a Standalone command 60 minutes (§9.5).
- When hyp runs a Drive, Evidence or Standalone command for the operator and the script exits non-zero, hyp stops there and exits with that code unchanged, so a check that exits 30 can be told apart from hyp's own 1 (refusal), 2 (bad arguments) and 3 (environment). A command that times out or is killed by a signal has no exit code, and hyp exits 3. hyp's own refusals come before any command starts and leave no row, so the record always tells a script's exit from hyp's; a script whose code alone must tell it apart exits 10 or above.

### 9.4 Records

- **Sandbox record.** `hyp sandbox create` writes `sandbox.json`, and only hyp writes it; `hyp sandbox remove` copies it to OUT_DIR. Each command's output goes to `recipe.log` after a `== REF step: command` line. The fields are listed under "The sandbox record" in `RECIPE-FORMAT.md`. Its `commands` list holds each command hyp ran in the sandbox (Launch, Doctor, Drive, Cleanup), in order, with its step, its arguments and its exit code; `hyp sandbox drive` adds to it.
- **Command record.** For each run of Evidence or Standalone commands, hyp writes a command record in the new directory that `--record DIR` names (refused with exit 2 if it exists, is or resolves inside a `recipes/` directory the recipe lookup searches, or, for Evidence, inside OUT_DIR, comparing directories by identity so symlinks and other spellings do not get past it; with exit 3 if its path cannot be resolved): `command.json`, naming the recipe ref, its hash, the library path, the step and the working directory, with one row per command (its arguments, its exit code or why it has none, and when it ran) and `arg_sha256`, the sha256 of each file an operator argument names; `command.log`, the output after `== REF step: command` lines; and each check's product, its stdout in `stdout` and its `$HYP_OUT` tree in `out/` (Standalone), or `stdout/<n>` and `out/<n>/` (Evidence command `n`), kept even when the check fails (ADR 0003). The fields are listed under "The command record" in `RECIPE-FORMAT.md`.
- **Argument hashes.** `command.json` (format 3) holds `arg_sha256`, mapping each operator argument of `hyp recipe run` or `hyp recipe evidence` that is an absolute path to a regular file, alone or as the VALUE of a `KEY=VALUE` word, symlinks followed, to that file's sha256. hyp hashes them before the first command runs, so the record names the input, not what a command rewrote. It is bound at run time, not when the Experiment is added. Limits: a directory (such as Evidence's OUT_DIR) and a relative path are not hashed, and neither is a file the command reads without being given it, which its `External:` line names. The key is absent when no argument names a file.
- **Known answers.** Each recipe entry of `sandbox.json`, and `command.json`, holds `known_answers`: `hyp_sha256`, the hyp that ran the cases, and `cases`, one `name` and `outcome` per case (§7.6). Each case's stderr goes to `known-answers.log` after a `== REF known answer NAME` line: in the sandbox, kept in OUT_DIR on remove, and in the command record's directory (ADR 0002).
- **Format.** `sandbox.json` and `command.json` each carry `"format"`, the shape number of that file (ADR 0002). A golden test per file fails `go test` when its shape changes without a new number, so a reader can compare the number before reading the rest. A record without the key was written before it.
- **Changes.** When create finishes, hyp writes `manifest.json` in the sandbox, a list of every path in `wt/` with its size, mode and hash. `hyp sandbox remove` diffs `wt/` against it and writes `changes.json` (format 1) to OUT_DIR, with the added and modified files up to 10 MB under `changes/`. The fields are listed under "Changes" in `RECIPE-FORMAT.md`.
- **Writes.** hyp writes `sandbox.json` and `command.json` to a temporary file in the same directory and renames it over the record, so a reader sees the old record or the new one, never part of one. A hyp killed between the two leaves a `.sandbox.json-*` or `.command.json-*` file that nothing reads; a sandbox's goes with it at remove.
- **Rows.** hyp writes each command's row before the command starts and rewrites it when the command ends. A row with no `ended` (and so no `exit` or `error`) is a command hyp stopped during: hyp was killed, or the machine stopped. Its output so far is in the log. When the write before a command fails, the command does not run and hyp exits 3, except under Cleanup, which runs every command anyway and reports the failed write as a failed Cleanup. A remove refused for a leftover process keeps the Cleanup rows it ran, and each recipe's `cleanup`, in the sandbox's record.
- **One hyp command per sandbox.** `hyp sandbox create`, `drive` and `remove` hold a lock on `sandbox.lock` in the sandbox while they run. A second one on the same sandbox is refused with exit 3, naming the hyp command that holds it, and changes nothing. The lock goes away when its hyp exits, however it exits. `hyp recipe evidence` and `hyp recipe run` take no lock, because each writes only the new directory it made.

### 9.5 Choices

The open choices were decided in a hyp tree (#150 set it up and #151 tested it, in `investigations/recipe-commands`, kept at commit 97219b1) and while building (#152, #163, #164).

1. How a Standalone command is named: an inline label, `Run NAME: ./script WORDS` (#151, R-TZCSA4). The owner picked it over a heading; both resolved every real use.
2. How the operator hyp is checked: by a Doctor command in the harness recipe (#151, R-1BVVQF), so hyp records no operator fields. Accepted limits: an Experiment under `--recipe none` gets no check, and each recipe that needs it carries the check.
3. One recipe format (ADR 0002, #205). The reach test, which froze a bundle holding a script no command named, was deleted: the known-answer gate proves what a verdict script gives, while a reach test only proved that a script was named. Every file other than a command's script is hashed content, hashing never parses, and a bundle is `frozen` once a tree pins it and `draft` before.
4. The Drive command is `hyp sandbox drive ID` (#152). The name is the step, as create runs Launch and Doctor and remove runs Cleanup. With no operator arguments, the recipe's fixed words and its inputs decide a drive.
5. `hyp sandbox remove` does not run scripted Evidence; `hyp recipe evidence` runs it, the first time and every time (#152). One path serves the first run and every re-run, a later version is only another REF, and remove's own exit codes never mix with a check's.
6. Timeouts (#152): Drive and Standalone 60 minutes per command, because the longest kept create-to-remove was 11.6 minutes and a re-test script drives sandboxes itself; Evidence 10 minutes per command, because it only reads kept files.
7. The command record is a directory the operator names with `--record` (#152), so it can sit under `.tree/evidence/<E-id>/` and be cited, and large output stays in its log. The commands run from a temporary copy, so a script cannot change the library version it ran from.
8. (replaced by choice 3)
9. A busy sandbox is refused, not waited for (#163). A Drive can run 60 minutes, a waiting hyp would hang its caller silently, and queueing is job-runner work §9.2 rules out. The lock is an flock inside the sandbox, so the kernel frees it when hyp dies and it is deleted with the sandbox.
10. An interrupted command leaves a row with no `ended` (#163). Every command hyp runs is a row (§9.2), and only a row written before the command starts survives a kill. A finished row is unchanged.
11. hyp does not clean up a killed run's temporary copy (#163). It holds nothing the library does not, and a sweep of another hyp's directories would be a reaper.
12. A record DIR inside OUT_DIR is refused (#164). The check reads OUT_DIR, its record is written before each command starts, and a re-run must read the same files as the first run. A record beside OUT_DIR, the documented place, is unaffected.
13. A record DIR inside any `recipes/` directory the lookup searches is refused, not only one inside the ref's own bundle (#164). A record changes the hash of whatever bundle it lands in, an outer copy of the ref must hash the same as the nearest, and a record in a `recipes/` directory that does not exist yet would start a library the lookup finds.
14. (replaced by choice 3)

        os.remove(p)

        shutil.rmtree(p)

for sk in g.SKILLS:
    src = os.path.join(wt, "skills", sk)
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(src, "SKILL.md")):
        g.die("launch: the commit has no skills/%s/SKILL.md" % sk, 1)
    shutil.move(src, os.path.join(wt, ".claude", "skills", sk))
if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(wt, "skills")) and not os.listdir(os.path.join(wt, "skills")):
    os.rmdir(os.path.join(wt, "skills"))

if inputs["arm"] != "base":
    for sk in sorted(os.listdir(inputs["variant"])):
        dst = os.path.join(wt, ".claude", "skills", sk, "SKILL.md")

}
with open(os.path.join(tmp, "state.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(state, f, indent=1, sort_keys=True)
    f.write("\n")
print("launch: arm %s trial %s, %d skill files, %d events at the cut" % (
    state["arm"], state["trial"], len(state["skill_files"]), len(cut_ids)))

import time

import gatelib as g

TIMEOUT = 50 * 60

wt = os.environ["HYP_SANDBOX_WT"]
tmp = os.environ["HYP_SANDBOX_RECIPE_TMP"]
inputs = g.read_inputs(os.environ["HYP_SANDBOX_INPUTS"])
if os.path.exists(os.path.join(tmp, "summary.json")):
    g.die("drive: this sandbox was driven already; one sandbox is one trial", 1)

env = dict(os.environ)
env["HYP_ACTOR"] = "runner-%s" % inputs["trial"]
for k in ("HYP_SANDBOX_INPUTS", "HYP_SANDBOX_RECIPE_TMP"):
    env.pop(k, None)
cmd = ["claude", "-p", "--model", "sonnet", "--setting-sources", "project",
       "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions", "--output-format", "stream-json",
       "--verbose", "--no-session-persistence"]
t0 = time.time()
timed_out = False
with open(inputs["brief"], "rb") as brief, \
        open(os.path.join(tmp, "transcript.jsonl"), "wb") as out:
    try:
        p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=wt, env=env, stdin=brief, stdout=out,
                             start_new_session=True)
    except OSError as e:
        g.die("drive: cannot start claude: %s" % e, 1)
    try:
        code = p.wait(timeout=TIMEOUT)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        code = None
    try:
        os.killpg(p.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
    except OSError:
        pass
    if timed_out:
        p.wait()

turns = cost = None
for m in g.read_jsonl(os.path.join(tmp, "transcript.jsonl")):
    if m.get("type") == "result":
        turns, cost = m.get("num_turns"), m.get("total_cost_usd")
summary = {"format": 1, "exit": code, "timed_out": timed_out, "turns": turns,
           "cost_usd": cost, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}
with open(os.path.join(tmp, "summary.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(summary, f, indent=1, sort_keys=True)
    f.write("\n")

ev = subprocess.run(["hyp", "events", "--json"], cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True)
with open(os.path.join(tmp, "events.json"), "w") as f:
    f.write(ev.stdout if ev.returncode == 0 else json.dumps({"format": 1, "events": [], "error": ev.stderr}))
print("drive: %s" % json.dumps(summary, sort_keys=True))

content.text:
The instrument is built as `recipes/skill-gate@1/`. `hyp recipe known-answers skill-gate@1` passes all 23 cases, and `hyp recipe check` shows no drift and no warnings for it. I have not run `hyp add exp --recipe skill-gate@1`. The bundle is still a draft, since no tree pins it yet.

**Smoke test:** Launch, Doctor, Drive, Cleanup, remove and the scoring command all ran in a throwaway sandbox. It used a scratch store, a trivial brief and one real `claude` call, with no tree created in this repository. That run exercised the plumbing only: the runner loaded no skill, so the fingerprint and end-state logic ran only on the hand-written known-answer fixtures. I removed the sandbox and the scratch files afterwards.

**Bundle:**
- **Launch:** strips `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude`, `plans`, `METHOD.md`, `.agentkit` and `investigations/` from the sandbox. It moves the two skills into `.claude/skills/` and lays the arm's variant `SKILL.md` files over them. It records the event ids at the store cut.
- **Doctor:** checks that sandbox is as described (no agent files, skills as recorded, events equal to the cut, `hyp` runs, `claude` on the `PATH`).
- **Drive:** starts a fresh `claude -p --model sonnet` runner on the brief, with project settings only. It stops the runner after 50 minutes and keeps the transcript, a run summary and the tree's events. A runner that fails or times out still counts as a trial.
- **Evidence:** `./score.py` prints the seven `key<TAB>value` lines from the method for one trial.
- **Standalone:** `verdict` takes the rows and all score files, needs exactly 5 trials per arm with distinct numbers, and prints `verdict: repro=…` plus one line per variant arm.
- **Known answers:** 6 score cases and 17 verdict cases. They cover every field, both fingerprints, `end_state` recorded, registered and none, and every verdict branch. They also cover the unloaded-skill rules, the k=1/2/3 boundaries, and the refusal cases.
